Biblical Marriage
BIB-li-kuhl MAR-ij
doctrinal phrase
From biblical (according to Scripture) and marriage (Old French mariage, the wedded estate); the covenant union God ordained at creation.

📖 Biblical Definition

Biblical marriage is the lifelong covenant union of one man and one woman before God, ordained by the Creator at the beginning, before the fall and before any nation or church, as the first and most fundamental of human institutions. God made them male and female, and said, “Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh.” The Lord Jesus reaffirmed this creation pattern against the loose divorce practice of His day, returning to Genesis: “What therefore God hath joined together, let not man put asunder.” Marriage is thus a divine institution, not a human invention to be redefined at will; its terms are fixed by the God who made it. It is the union of two sexes, male and female, the only category of legitimate sexual union; it is monogamous, one man and one woman; it is a covenant, entered by vow before God and binding for life; and it is ordered, with the husband as head and the wife as helper, reflecting the order of creation. Marriage also bears a sacred typology: it images the union of Christ and His church, the husband’s sacrificial headship picturing Christ’s love and the wife’s glad submission picturing the church’s. The dictionary holds biblical marriage as the creational and unchangeable standard, the foundation of the family and of society, given by God for companionship, the bearing and rearing of godly children, and the picture of the gospel.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The lifelong covenant union of one man and one woman before God, ordained at creation, the only legitimate sexual union, ordered as a picture of Christ and His church.

BIBLICAL MARRIAGE, the covenant union of one man and one woman before God.

Ordained by the Creator at the beginning, the first of human institutions.

“A man shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh.”

Monogamous, lifelong, and ordered, with the husband as head and the wife as helper.

A picture of the union of Christ and His church.

📖 Key Scripture

Gen 2:24 — "Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh."

Mat 19:6 — "Wherefore they are no more twain, but one flesh. What therefore God hath joined together, let not man put asunder."

Eph 5:31 — "For this cause shall a man leave his father and mother, and shall be joined unto his wife, and they two shall be one flesh."

Heb 13:4 — "Marriage is honourable in all, and the bed undefiled: but whoremongers and adulterers God will judge."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Marriage is severed from its creation design and redefined by the will of man to include unions Scripture forbids.

expand to see more

The reigning corruption is the redefinition of marriage by the will of man—the claim that marriage is a social construct to be reshaped at will, so that two men or two women may be “married,” or that the sexes themselves may be denied. Scripture forecloses this: God made them male and female and joined the man to his wife, and the Lord Jesus anchored marriage in that unchangeable creation order. What God has defined, no court, culture, or church may redefine; the union of two persons of the same sex is no marriage but a violation of the creation ordinance, and the denial of the two sexes is a corruption of Genesis itself.

A second corruption is the cheapening of marriage even where its form is kept—cohabitation that refuses the covenant, easy divorce that breaks it, and a contractual view that treats it as a temporary arrangement of mutual convenience. The dictionary holds marriage as God made it: a lifelong covenant of one man and one woman, ordered and exclusive, honorable in all, and the appointed picture of Christ and His church. To redefine it is to attack the gospel it images and the society it founds; the church’s task is not to follow the age but to hold and honor the creation ordinance.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

The phrase names the creation ordinance of marriage—one man, one woman, one flesh, for life, before God.

expand to see more

Hebrew dābaq — to cleave, cling; the man “shall cleave unto his wife.”

Hebrew basār ’eḥād — “one flesh,” the union of husband and wife.

Greek gameo — to marry; gamos — marriage, wedding.

Instituted at creation, before the fall, the first human institution.

A type of the union of Christ and His church (Ephesians 5).

Usage

"Biblical marriage is upheld as the union of one man and one woman against redefinition."

"Christ’s appeal to Genesis grounds marriage in the unchangeable creation order."

"Its typology of Christ and the church is preached in weddings and on Ephesians 5."
